title: Add the Release Radar demo app
problem: Teams want one page that shows what each repository shipped this week. Add a new Outfitter app, Release Radar, at apps/release-radar: an Astro app built like apps/hr (the reference app in this repository, which uses the SDK's outfitterApp integration instead of its own middleware), demo mode only, serving staged data. It uses the SDK packages in packages/ through the npm workspace; do not change packages/ or apps/hr.

acceptanceCriteria.text: apps/release-radar/app.json has id outfitter/release-radar, version 0.1.0, runtime cloudflare-workers-for-platforms, dataLocation managing-outfitter-instance, a demo mode with no capabilities, and catalog access demo-only with demo slug release-radar and name Release Radar.

apps/release-radar/package.json is @ai-outfitter/app-release-radar version 0.1.0 with outfitter.kind app, depends on astro, @astrojs/cloudflare and the SDK packages like apps/hr, and has dev (astro dev), build (outfitter-app-build --mode demo), check (astro check), test and test:unit (node:test) scripts.

src/fixtures.ts exports repositories: at least three staged repositories, each with a name and the pull requests merged this week (number, title, author, mergedAt), and a summarize(repositories) function returning, per repository, its name and merged pull request count, sorted by count descending.
The page at / has the heading Release Radar and lists every staged repository with its merged pull request count, each linking to /repos/<name>.
The page at /repos/<name> lists that repository's merged pull requests with number, title and author; an unknown repository name responds 404.

astro.config.mjs registers the SDK's outfitterApp integration (@ai-outfitter/app-sdk/astro) like apps/hr, with app release-radar, readOnly and the same contentSecurityPolicy as apps/hr; the app has no src/middleware.ts of its own. So GET /__health answers {"app":"release-radar","status":"ok"}, methods other than GET and HEAD get 405, and built pages carry that Content-Security-Policy and Cache-Control: private, no-store.
A node:test unit test in apps/release-radar/tests covers summarize, and the repository's npm test passes (it builds every app's demo package and runs its unit tests).
